newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity mixed in thin, range-bound trade.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity mixed in thin, range-bound trade.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were trading mixed Tuesday in a quiet session that was mostly range-bound with little fundamental news, industry sources said.

As of 1215 EDT, NYMEX September Palo Verde (PV) was trading up one cent at $30.45 per megawatt hour (MWh) following exchanges at $30.15-30.70, while October was up 15 cents at the day's high of $23.75 after reaching a low of $23.60 per MWh.
"PV is kind of stuck in a range (of $30.00-30.60)," said one Houston-based power trader.

September California Oregon Border (COB) was down 44 cents at the day's low of $22.55 following trade as high as $22.75, while October was down 15 cents at the day's high of $22.40 following exchange as low as $22.25 per MWh.
NYMEX volumes were not available, but sources said trade was relatively quiet.

In Western electricity news, the 3,800 megawatt (MW) AC segment of the Pacific Intertie was scheduled to be curtailed to 2,950 MW between 0800-1600 PDT through Friday, while the DC line will be limited to 2,360 over the same period.
A high pressure ridge building in the West was expected to heat the region's temperatures three to seven degrees Fahrenheit above normal through Friday, meteorologists said.

In its latest six to 10 day forecast, Weather Services Corp said temperatures would average below normal along the coastal region, near normal further inland and above normal in the eastern part of the Southwest.

The 1,221 MW unit 2 at the Palo Verde generating complex in Arizona continued to coast down toward its refueling outage in September. The unit, in Wintersburg, Ariz., was operating at 80 percent power early Tuesday.
Separately, NYMEX said Monday it proposed to change the opening times for the electricity futures contracts beginning Wednesday, Sept 3.
The start time will be changed to 0955 EDT/1355 GMT from 1030 EDT/1430 GMT, pending approval by the Commodity Futures Trading Commission.
COB open interest for August 18 fell 28 to 5,264 while PV open interest rose 73 to 5,677, NYMEX said.
